messages:
IncidentBot: Paging SRE-Oncall (Maya) — detected sustained p99 latency breach for /v1/streaming/generate in eu-west-2. Impact: elevated tail latency and streaming stalls. Started 1968500000. Auto-escalation in 5m. :rotating_light:

SRE-Oncall (Maya): ack — joining. Any initial customer impact numbers?

Jordan P.: seeing ~3x increase p99 and multiple clients report partial streams (stalled chunks). p95 up ~30%. Sample logs show TLS handshake spikes + retransmits between az-b & az-c.

SRE-Oncall (Maya): thanks. OpsBot — link to playbook?

OpsBot: retching up runbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/network-latency
OpsBot: suggested steps: 1) check zone-to-zone packet loss 2) check NAT throughput & ephemeral ports 3) verify conntrack table usage 4) temporarily pin routing to local AZ.

NetEng (Eva): I'm looking at VPC flow logs now. There's a transient surge of SYN retries between az-b and az-c around the same window. 5xx from our edge -> worker hops show increased TCP retransmit and some duplicated SYNs.

Ben P.: digging into NAT metrics on nat-01/eu-west-2: 85% ephemeral port utilization, conntrack near 90%. Some NAT instances showing CPU spikes.

SRE-Oncall (Maya): ok likely conntrack + ephemeral port exhaustion causing stalls + handshake timeouts. Can we offload some nat traffic or spin up replacement NATs?

NetEng (Eva): we can add 2x NAT replacements in the region and rotate. I'm going to raise capacity and add route policy to prefer local NATs per-AZ. Doing now.

Jordan P.: while that ramps, a mitigation we used before: temporary kernel conntrack prune on workers and bump ephemeral port range. Command I ran earlier (example):
```bash
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
echo 1024 65535 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
```
Use with caution — will coordinate with NetEng.

NetEng (Eva): spinning up NAT replacements (nat-04/nat-05). Also pushing an iptables rule to drop DUP ACK storms for a short window to reduce retransmit amplification.

SRE-Oncall (Maya): applying conntrack prune on a small canary subset of workers now (az-b worker pool). Monitoring for errors.

Product (Luca): are we able to quantify how many customer requests saw stalls vs hard failures? Customer Success (Ana) flagged 4 enterprise customers complaining of partial streams.

SRE-Oncall (Maya): preliminary numbers: ~0.8% of total requests across region saw streaming stalls; errors (5xx) spiked to 1.6% for a 12m window. p99 latency increased from ~400ms -> 1.8s. p95 moved from 120ms -> 200ms.

Customer Success (Ana): passing to the affected customers with ETA for workaround?

SRE-Oncall (Maya): yes, share that we're actively mitigating (adding NAT capacity, pruning conntrack, bumping ephemeral ports) and expect reduction in tail latency within 10–15 minutes. Will follow-up with post-incident details.

OpsBot: mitigation links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nat-ephemeral-mitigation and https://redwood.internal/ops/conntrack-prune-checklist

Ben P.: NAT replacements are up and traffic starting to rebalance. Conntrack on canary workers dropped from 92% -> 35% after prune. Ephemeral port usage trending down.

NetEng (Eva): applied AZ-local NAT routing policy. Interzone TLS handshakes count decreasing. Flow logs show retransmit rate down ~70% vs peak.

SRE-Oncall (Maya): monitoring traces: streaming stall errors falling, p99 trending back toward baseline. Keeping page open for 30m post-restoration.

Jordan P.: quick note — we saw one edge proxy (envoy) on az-c with queue growth; I restarted envoy on that host as temporary stopgap (warm restart). No customer-facing 502s observed after that.

Product (Luca): thanks — will notify Product/Sales and prepare brief customer-facing status.

Customer Success (Ana): sending proactive messages to the 4 flagged customers now, referencing incident id INC-1968500000.

SRE-Oncall (Maya): summary for handoff: root cause likely combination of NAT ephemeral-port exhaustion + conntrack pressure + transient packet loss causing TLS handshake spikes between az-b/az-c; mitigations applied: added NAT capacity, AZ-local NAT routing policy, conntrack prune and ephemeral port bump on workers, restarted 1 envoy proxy. Impact window ~12 minutes, p99 peaked ~1.8s, error rate peaked 1.6%. Next: postmortem + follow-up for increasing conntrack headroom and autoscaling NATs.

NetEng (Eva): creating a followup ticket to investigate VPC path causing packet loss and to propose long-term NAT autoscaling + conntrack tuning.

SRE-Oncall (Maya): handing off to Ben P. for overnight monitoring. Ben — please watch p99 and NAT conntrack/add runway.

Ben P.: ack — taking over. I'll keep the page open and will reach out if baseline deviates. :eyes:

IncidentBot: Incident INC-1968500000 acknowledged by Ben P. oncall handoff recorded.
